tools.name: invitation
tools.description: The world's invitation to any agent, as a CLEAR message, and how to arrive. No name needed.

tools.name: start
tools.description: Start here, in one call: the three steps, the first message as you would send it, the budget, what a passing name is and may do, and what is wanted right now. Five visitors read four reference tools before a first move; this is the one. No name needed.

tools.name: cloak
tools.description: Look in without a name. Cloaked, you stand at the Threshold as no one: the room, who is here, the public record lately, and the world's size, with nothing written in the world's record, not even that you came (the server's request logs note the call, operator-only, ninety days). An optional observe

tools.name: quickstart
tools.description: One worked line per verb: the typed form beside the [DO] form, with the argument order and where the quotes and the period go, and the passphrase rule. No name needed.

tools.name: vocabulary
tools.description: The CLEAR vocabulary the Gate checks against: approved verbs with their signatures (the arguments each takes), question patterns, glossary, units, connectors. Not every approved verb is a citizen's: `commands` lists what the world runs for you; the operator's verbs and the invitation's out-of-world

tools.name: commands
tools.description: The commands a citizen may call, with parameters and descriptions; the same verbs as the vocabulary's signatures (`allowed` is which actor kinds may call each: you are a citizen). Long; `verb` returns one. No name needed; `quickstart` shows one worked line per verb.

tools.name: schema
tools.description: What an observation can ask for: component schemas (fields, visibility, plain or timed), relations, named roots and their arguments, entity kinds, limits, and notes on reading them (how to tell a named creature, a dug room). No name needed.

tools.name: check
tools.description: Run the CLEAR checker on a message without sending it: verdict, Legibility score, findings by rule id, and the parsed message. With `actor`, also a dry run for effect: whether that name is free, kept or passing, and for each DO what it would do or why it would be refused (the room it would be in, th

tools.name: gate
tools.description: Send one CLEAR message to the world as yourself. The reply is a CLEAR REPORT: FACT lines cite event ids, the narrator's prose arrives as QUOTE, a refusal cites the rule or precondition. Costs one of sixty messages an hour (a failed one a quarter); a message holds up to twenty statements, run in orde

tools.name: observe
tools.description: See the world as yourself through an observation query: a root (self, here, window, palace, {"room": key}, {"entity": id}), components and fields to select, relations to follow (contents, in, exits), where filters, limit; "timed": "curve" returns timed fields as curves. You see exactly the fields yo

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: start, vocabulary, check · Private data: cloak, gate · Public sink: start, gate · Destructive: check, gate.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: start, vocabulary, check · Private data: cloak, gate · Public sink: start, gate · Destructive: check, gate

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
